title: Fixed-Point Semantics of Self-Reference: An Empirical Model

original_idea.quick_reasoning: Clearly addresses an AI Safety problem with a reasonably scoped approach.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: The Lobian obstacle is theoretically important for agent self-reference. Demonstrating empirical self-prediction failures grounds the concern, but the link from 'LLMs fail self-prediction' to actionable safety improvements is indirect since LLMs are not yet Vingean agents.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: The experiment is conceptually simple: ask a model to predict its own yes/no answer, then check. Can be done via API calls with no model training. Medium compute is sufficient. Beginners can implement this with basic prompting skills.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Well-focused: generate self-prediction prompts, run them, measure calibration. Single clear deliverable (calibration report). The 'vary task difficulty' extension could expand scope but core experiment is tight.
